criteria.name: Introduction: mission concept and rationale. Include the following required information: What is the spacecraft's primary mission? Why is the mission needed? How many spacecraft are used and why? Who are the users (operator and customers)?
criteria.reasoning: All required introductory elements are thoroughly addressed. The rationale is clearly established, user roles (operator and end users) are explicitly defined, and the single-spacecraft architecture is well justified.

evidence.quote: The primary mission of ZYZZsat is to image the whole Great Barrier Reef in visible bands at 5 m resolution
The operator is the Australian Institute of Marine Science (AIMS), which already runs the long-term monitoring program for the reef

criteria.name: Main body: mission design. Present a summary of the mission design using software and/or hand calculations as appropriate. Include relevant screenshots and software files in the main body of the report and/or appendix. Include the following information: Where will it launch from, and using which launch vehicle? Why did you choose this option? What type of orbit will you use? What are its characteristics and orbital elements? Will you need to perform any orbital maneuvers? Which ground control facilities will you use? How often will your spacecraft be able to communicate with ground control? How long will the mission last, and what are your plans for EOL?
criteria.reasoning: The mission design demonstrates an exceptional standard of technical rigour. Launch vehicle and site selection, orbit determination (verified via J2 hand calculations and STK), ground communications access analysis, data budgeting, and end-of-life decay mechanics are comprehensively covered and supported by clear figures and data tables.

evidence.quote: The baseline is an SSMS rideshare flight on Vega C from Kourou in early 2025
The EOL plan is therefore passive: a drag sail is deployed at the end of the mission.

criteria.name: Conclusion
criteria.reasoning: The conclusion provides an excellent, nuanced synthesis of the mission outcomes alongside a critical appraisal of technical limitations and concrete pathways for future work.

evidence.quote: ZYZZsat meets the mission needs set out in the introduction with one 50 kg satellite.
The design has four limitations. First, Vega C has not yet flown, so the Falcon 9 rideshare service is kept as a fallback

criteria.name: Report presentation
criteria.reasoning: The presentation is exemplary. It contains a well-structured executive summary, clear figure/table labelling, immaculate IEEE-style citation formatting, and detailed documentation of software models in the appendix.

overall: An outstanding, professional engineering submission. The technical calculations, trade-offs, and STK modelling are executed with exceptional clarity, precision, and completeness.

feedback.summary: You submitted an outstanding, professional engineering report that met all rubric requirements to the highest standard. Your mission concept, technical justifications, orbital mechanics calculations, and software verification were exceptionally detailed, cohesive, and clearly documented.
next_steps: Consider conducting sensitivity analyses on drag-sail deployment reliability to further robustify your end-of-life plan.
Develop the secondary payload or Falcon 9 fallback operational profile to mitigate primary launch vehicle uncertainty.
Explore multi-ground-station networks to evaluate whether downlink latency could be reduced during peak reef-monitoring seasons.

criteria.C1: You achieved the Accomplished level by clearly establishing the ZYZZsat mission rationale, defining user roles (AIMS and stakeholders), and thoroughly justifying your single-satellite architecture in Section 1. To maintain this high standard, continue supporting user operational requirements with direct quantitative data needs.
criteria.C2: You reached the Accomplished level through exceptional technical rigour in Section 2. You supported your launch vehicle selection, analytical J2 orbital hand calculations, STK modelling, and passive deorbit drag-sail strategy with clear evidence and verification. For future work, consider modelling stochastic atmospheric drag variations during deorbit.
criteria.C3: You achieved Accomplished in Section 3 by providing a concise synthesis of mission objectives alongside an honest, critical appraisal of key design limitations (such as Vega C flight heritage). To build on this, include high-level cost or schedule risk mitigations in future work.
criteria.C4: Your presentation reached the Accomplished level through a clear engineering layout, a concise executive summary, consistent tabular and graphical presentation, immaculate referencing, and complete STK model documentation in Appendix A. Continue using this professional formatting standard for future engineering deliverables.
